title: Fantasy Playoff Weeks 19 to 21 (Ending 2027-03-28)
markdown:
**Summary.** For our league, the playoff schedule (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28) should only break ties at the auction, and only between similar expensive players. The one schedule factor that really matters is a two-game week during the playoffs. Most of the playoff edge comes later, from trades made before the 2027-03-04 deadline and from heavy streaming in March.

## Use the March 28 schedule

Our season ends Sunday 2027-03-28, and that is the end date the experts recommend. Yahoo's default end is April 4. When a note or a schedule tool gives two versions, always read the March 28 one. Before you look at any schedule, confirm our playoff weeks in the league settings: weeks 19, 20 and 21. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=2029), [10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1877), [09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1670), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=88), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=435))

The experts say ending in late March is now safer than before. One speaker used to suggest March 21. The lottery and tanking reforms should mean less resting and more competitive late March games. One note counted about eight or nine teams tanking or resting players last season, and expects this season's playoffs to be less extreme. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=2141), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=372), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1964), [09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1733), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=144))

## Two-game playoff weeks are what matters

A two-game week during weeks 19, 20 or 21 is the schedule factor that actually matters. Leave those teams aside and the schedules are mostly comparable. They should not change player values much. Do not agonize over 12 versus 11 playoff games, because too much can change by March. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=2054), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1958))

Back-to-backs inside the playoff weeks matter more than a team's back-to-back total for the season. Check them when you compare two teams' playoff schedules. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=893), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1906))

One note says Minnesota has a two-game week in the middle of the fantasy playoffs whatever weeks a head-to-head league uses. That makes it hard to avoid. Check where it falls in our March 28 schedule before you use it to separate two players. ([08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1933))

A top-two seed with a first-round bye can absorb a two-game week in the first playoff week. Check whether our playoff format gives byes. If it does, a week 19 two-game week is the least harmful one. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1361))

## At the auction: a tiebreaker for expensive players

At the draft, the playoff schedule is the least important factor. Use it only to choose between two players you value about the same. Never buy a worse player because his playoff schedule is better. A clear talent gap always wins. Player value is too uncertain for anything more: players picked around 100 often finish around 30, and players picked around 20 can finish around 60. ([09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1983), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1978), [08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=416), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=187))

Schedule matters mostly for early picks, meaning the first three rounds. In our 12-team auction, read that as the 36 or so most expensive players. You do not want your best player to have a two-game week in the semifinals or the final. For mid-priced and cheap players, ignore the schedule and bid on talent and role. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1848), [09-29](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1879), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1797))

In practice: if two stars are close on your board and one has a two-game playoff week, bid a little less on him. If he is still on the board late in the auction at a clear discount and there is no better option, buy him. Do not chase him early at full price. ([08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1942), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1522))

Rostering several players from the same NBA team is fine, probably up to three. That is easier to accept when the team has no two-game playoff weeks. Five is too many. Do not build the roster around playoff game counts. ([09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=364), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=187))

## Where the experts differ

The notes do not fully agree on how hard to downgrade a two-game playoff week. One side calls it a real penalty: in head-to-head leagues, a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board, and it is the schedule factor that counts. The other side says playoff schedules are the least important draft factor, should only break ties between equal players, and should not drive your draft plan. The common ground for us: move such a player down a little among similar options, mostly among the expensive ones, and never pass on a clearly better player for it. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1665), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1983), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150), [08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1942))

## In season: trade for games, then stream

Playoff games matter more as the season goes on. Trades that improve your schedule, such as adding playoff games or getting rid of a two-game playoff week, are worth considering in season, not at the draft. Our trade deadline is 2027-03-04, more than two weeks before week 19. Do your schedule trades before then. Trades are common here, so offer a similar player with a better playoff schedule for one with a two-game week. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1408), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1993))

The season has three phases: discovery early, optimizing in the middle, and maximizing near the end and in the playoffs. In the maximizing phase, drop stashed or injured players and stream as much as you can. Our limit is 6 acquisitions per week with daily FAB, so plan each playoff week's adds around which teams play the most games and back-to-backs that week. Keep some FAB for March. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1712), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1993), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=893))

A head-to-head playoff matchup needs only 5 category wins out of 9. Even balanced teams end up punting something in the playoffs. Point your streaming at the categories you can win that week, and stop worrying about the ones you cannot. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=454))
